body.notes:
OUTCOME inconclusive: Part A PASS on all 7 hosts; Part B INCONCLUSIVE on all 7 hosts (overall = inconclusive: no part failed, B did not pass). Neither amendment triggers.

HOSTS (7): verifier local Intel Xeon @2.10GHz x86-64 (exit 0, valid=true, problems=[]); CI run 42172779341 at commit 3be61b207666325ac2bd1fdee66afa1a503d2935: ubuntu-24.04-1 and -2 AMD EPYC 7763, ubuntu-24.04-3 Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, ubuntu-24.04-arm-1/2/3 arm64 CPU part 0xd49 (Neoverse N2). Every CI scoreboard: valid=true, problems=[], plan sha256 177547d8..., rounds 30, seed 20261106, all five weights retrained byte-identically in the jail, numpy 2.5.3, gcc 13.3.0. CI exit codes are not recorded (the workflow pipes through tee || true); exit 0 is inferred from valid=true with no problems (loop.py returns 1 only with problems) and the 'wrote' line.

ACCURACY (identical on all 7 hosts; every candidate's predictions_sha256 identical across hosts; also reproduced by the verifier outside the jail by compiling each infer.c and recomputing from raw predictions): linear 1708/1797 = 0.950473; thermo 1725/1797 = 0.959933; mlp16 1724/1797 = 0.959377; mlp32 1735/1797 = 0.965498; mlp64 1727/1797 = 0.961046.
Paired diffs (d, SE as printed by evaluate; wins/losses on discordant images): mlp16-linear +0.008904 SE 0.002602 (19/3); mlp16-thermo -0.000556 SE 0.003099 (15/16); mlp32-linear +0.015025 SE 0.003458, z 4.35 (33/6); mlp32-thermo +0.005565 SE 0.003429, z 1.62 (24/14); mlp64-linear +0.010573 SE 0.002987, z 3.54 (24/5); mlp64-thermo +0.001113 SE 0.003340, z 0.33 (19/17).

PART A (mlp16), per host. Accuracy floor (host-independent): 0.959377 >= max(0.950473, 0.959933) - 0.005 = 0.954933, holds (margin 0.0044).
x86-64 (local Xeon, EPYC x2, Xeon 8573C; Ir/img linear 3888.19, thermo 3629.84, mlp16 720.37): cost vs linear 720.37/(0.959377-2*0.002602) = 754.97 < 3888.19/0.950473 = 4090.80, holds; vs thermo 720.37/(0.959377-2*0.003099) = 755.75 < 3629.84/0.959933 = 3781.34, holds; Ir ratio 720.37/3888.19 = 0.1853 and 720.37/3629.84 = 0.1985, both <= 0.5. PASS.
arm64 x3 (Ir/img linear 3141.74, thermo 2885.95, mlp16 835.19): vs linear 835.19/(0.959377-2*0.002602) = 875.30 < 3305.45, holds; vs thermo 835.19/(0.959377-2*0.003099) = 876.21 < 3006.41, holds; Ir ratio 0.2658 and 0.2894 <= 0.5. PASS.
Part A PASS on every host -> PASS.

PART B (mlp32, mlp64). Accuracy conditions are host-independent: mlp32 d > 2SE vs linear (0.015025 > 0.006916) but NOT vs thermo (0.005565 <= 0.006858); mlp64 d > 2SE vs linear (0.010573 > 0.005974) but NOT vs thermo (0.001113 <= 0.006679). So no candidate passes. Not FAIL either: every d(X,B) is > 0, and both mlp32 and mlp64 beat both baselines on cost past 2 SE on every host (x86-64: mlp32 1069.79 < 4090.80 and 1069.73 < 3781.34; mlp64 1763.12 < 4090.80 and 1764.42 < 3781.34; arm64: mlp32 1286.89 < 3305.45 and 1286.81 < 3006.41; mlp64 2145.84 < 3305.45 and 2147.42 < 3006.41). Rule: 'INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (e.g. positive differences but not past 2 SE)' -> Part B INCONCLUSIVE on every host. The binding comparison is mlp32 vs thermo, z = 1.62 (an exact McNemar on 24 vs 14 discordant images is not significant either). The validation-holdout edge over thermo (+1.05 pp, +1.15 pp) shrank to +0.56 pp and +0.11 pp on the 13 unseen writers.

AMENDMENT (1): all 7 hosts that ran the test command to completion gave valid=true, problems=[]; exit 0 locally. Disclosure: the verifier's FIRST local attempt (system python3 with numpy 2.5.3 but without sigstore/opentimestamps) exited 1 before any training or scoring, in require_plan: record.py check-anchors could not verify the Sigstore anchors without sigstore-python, so it reported 'entries 1-2 were never attested by the writer'. That is a missing verification dependency on the verifier's host, not a property of the plan: with a venv mirroring loop.yml (numpy==2.5.3 sigstore==4.5.1 opentimestamps-client==0.8.0) record.py verify and check-anchors both exit 0 (writer attested 1-2, OTS pending) and the same command exited 0. Its log is in evidence (test-local-attempt1-missing-sigstore.txt). If a stricter reader counts it under amendment (1), the outcome is still inconclusive. The command was otherwise run exactly as written, from /home/claude/exagium, plus only --out and --records.

AMENDMENT (2), code reading (all five, at the frozen digests): no finding.
train.py: loop/baselines/linear/train.py imports only sys, numpy (8-9), reads only its training-file argument via np.loadtxt(train_csv) (43), writes only argv[2] (51-53); its only constants are LAMBDAS and ITERS (11-12). loop/baselines/thermo/train.py: same shape, imports 44-45, np.loadtxt at 80, writes at 90-92, constants 47-48. loop/candidates/mlp16|32|64/train.py are identical except line 22 (H = 16/32/64): imports sys, numpy only (19-20); np.loadtxt(train_csv) at 129 is the only read; write at 142-146; constants SEED/EPOCHS/LAMBDAS 123-125 and the RNG is default_rng(SEED) (51). No file, network, env or os access; no embedded arrays, long literals or non-ASCII (max line 112 chars). Test-set data cannot enter except through code, and there is none.
infer.c: loop/baselines/linear/infer.c opens only argv[1] (9) and argv[2] (14), n = atol(argv[3]) (13); thermo/infer.c the same (8, 12, 11) and rejects pixels > 16 (17); mlp16|32|64/infer.c identical except line 12 (#define H), open argv[1] (24) and argv[2] (31), atol(argv[3]) (29), reject pixels > 16 (38-47). No getenv, /proc, cpuid/__builtin_cpu_*, clock/time/rdtsc, syscall, asm, dlopen or argv[0] use in any of them. The only data-dependent branches are on weights and input (argmax; mlp*/infer.c:73 skips zero hidden units, the same in counted and timed runs, cross-checked by predictions). GCC vector extensions compile to fixed SSE2/NEON with no -march, no run-time dispatch in candidate code. objdump of the verifier's x86-64 builds: the binaries call only fopen/fread/__fread_chk/fgetc/fclose/fwrite/malloc/strtol (memcpy/memset inlined); glibc's own internal CPU dispatch inside stdio is the harness's documented limit, not a candidate choice.

ODD / MINOR: (a) local Ir counts are exactly 1 higher than the three CI x86-64 hosts for every candidate (e.g. mlp16 1294500 vs 1294499), constant across candidates so likely a loader/kernel difference; no effect on any inequality. (b) The verifier's clone had a modified VERIFY.md and untracked loop/README.md not made by the verifier; neither is a frozen input (require_plan checked every frozen digest). (c) record.py check-anchors reports writer_code_changed=true between the runs that wrote entries 1 and 2 (informational). (d) Per the plan, SEs assume independent images; with 13 writers the true SEs are larger, which would only make B's accuracy shortfall vs thermo more pronounced. Native ns/img is not part of the verdict (local: linear 970.5, thermo 1208.2, mlp16 830.0, mlp32 894.3, mlp64 1117.3).
